title: Orchestrated pause/resume canary scheduler with dependency reconciliation
author: Leah Kim
release_notes: Adds pause/resume primitives to the canary scheduler and dependency reconciliation to avoid premature promotions. Backwards compatible with existing rollout manifests. Includes runbook and e2e tests.
description:
Motivation: We observed several production canary promotions where higher-level deployment dependencies (feature flags, schema migrations, and downstream service readiness) were not coordinated with the rollout controller. That led to partial promotions and manual intervention. This PR introduces a coordinated pause/resume scheduler that reconciles declared dependencies before advancing canary phases, and exposes explicit holdpoints for operator-driven interventions.

What this changes (single-string description): Adds a PauseResumeController to the orchestration layer that can place a canary in a persisted 'PAUSED' state, resume it when dependencies report ready, or auto-advance after timeouts. The controller evaluates a dependency graph declared in the Rollout CR: feature_flags, migration_jobs, downstream_service_endpoints. If any dependency reports unhealthy, the controller inserts a holdpoint and signals the mesh/router to stop traffic increases. Operators can add manual annotations to force a resume. The design intentionally separates evaluation (stateless) from action (idempotent transition writer) to keep the reconciliation loop observable and safe.

Key features: unified dependency model (declared as a list of typed references), holdpoints with reason codes and optional TTL, automatic soft-failback where the controller will attempt limited retries, optional backfill mode to re-run shadow traffic through the candidate model after resumed promotion, audit journal entries for each state transition, metrics and tracing for pause/resume decisions, and a small CLI helper (rolloutctl pause|resume|inspect).

Compatibility and upgrade notes: Existing Rollout manifests are untouched; the new dependency block is optional. Controllers older than this change will ignore the dependency block. We persist the controller's state in the existing rollout_status table using a new column (pause_state string) with a migration applied in a follow-up PR if the operator chooses to run the DB migration separately. No API breaking changes.

Testing and QA: Unit tests for the state transitions, property-based tests for the dependency graph evaluation, and an end-to-end scenario that exercises automated pause on simulated downstream outage and operator resume. Load tests show <4% scheduler latency increase at 5k rollouts/sec since the action writer is rate-limited and runs off the hot path.

Operational runbook summary (also added to docs/runbooks/canary-pause-resume.md): steps to identify paused rollouts, forcing a resume, inspecting decision traces, and reverting to previous model with snapshot replay.

Security: No new surface for remote control beyond existing operator RBAC. Rolloutctl commands require rollout:update scope.

Related: ENG-11234 (dependency-aware rollouts), ENG-11890 (pause/playback requirements), SUP-4421 (customer incident where migration and canary interleaving caused errors).

Merge disposition: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.

testing_summary: Local unit, integration, and e2e tests added. Fuzz tests generated for dependency graphs. Load test at 5k rollouts/s shows median reconcile latency increase from 14ms to 16ms. CI initially flaked on integration test due to fixture timeout and was rerun.
changelog_entry: Added pause/resume canary scheduler with dependency reconciliation, holdpoints, TTLs, audit journal entries, CLI helpers, and runbook.
notes_for_oncall: If you see persistent paused rollouts labeled 'migration:blocked' check the migration-job-controller logs and the dependency reporter. Use rolloutctl inspect <id> to view decision trace. To force resume: rolloutctl resume --force <id> (requires rollout:update scope).
security_review: No new permissions required beyond rollout:update. Reviewed by security team on 2026-02-20.
size_and_scope: Medium: controller + API types + CLI + docs + tests. Risk: medium due to DB change and operator-visible behavior; mitigations in runbook and migration plan.
upgrade_instructions: Optional DB migration to add pause_state can be applied before or after control plane upgrade. If you skip the migration, paused state will still be tracked in the transient decision trace. Recommended: apply migration in maintenance window and run backfill job provided in follow-up PR.
